title: The Ninth Configuration — What Science Actually Says #Shorts
description:
The unconscious does not argue with The Ninth Configuration; it simply acts first. The Ninth Configuration (also known as Twinkle, Twinkle, "Killer" Kane) is a 1980 American surrealist psychological drama film written, produced, and directed by William Peter Blatty, in his directorial debut. It is the second installment in Blatty's "Trilogy of Faith" after The Exorcist (1973), and followed by The Exorcist III (1990).

Reproduction explains more of The Ninth Configuration than any philosophy dares to admit. Blatty re-edited the film for its 1985 re-release, which was distributed by New World Pictures under the original title, The Ninth Configuration. On review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, The Ninth Configuration has an approval rating of 80% based on 15 reviews, with an average rating of 7/10.
